content.text: The text is a wide-ranging collection of Victorian essays, historical narrative, poetry, and children’s stories. Its essays advocate tolerance toward contemporaries, intellectual humility, honest scholarship, responsible writing, moral seriousness, and sympathy across classes and nationalities. They satirize vanity, plagiarism, excessive deference, bad temper, narrow definitions of morality, and contemptuous criticism. Historical sections describe the 1837 Lower Canada rebellion: Papineau’s agitation, Patriote resistance, battles at St Denis and St Charles, defeats at Moore’s Corners, and the attack on St Eustache. The poems explore love, loss, war, memory, exile, and Eastern settings. Brownie stories depict mischievous nocturnal adventures involving trains, balls, tugboats, race tracks, dinners, canals, studios, and village improvements. Sandra moved to the bedroom.
